analysis.title: Earnings Season Pulse: Strong deliveries don't offset pipeline risk
key_insights: AI-related companies kept reporting strong growth: AMD data-centre revenue +97% y/y, Super Micro raised its annual sales outlook to $72-82 billion, Palantir beat adjusted EPS estimates by 7%. The stocks still did not hold up, and Nasdaq fell 5% on 5 November, which SG attributes to increased regulatory risk from the US midterm elections.

European order books are not converting reliably into earnings. Alstom cut adjusted EBIT margin guidance from about 6.5% to ~1% and moved to a EUR1.5bn free cash outflow. Rheinmetall lowered its sales target for the second time in 2026 on programme delays. SG calls these company-specific but says they show the difficulty of turning infrastructure and defence backlogs into margins and cash flow.

Toyota raised operating-income guidance by 15% to JPY3.9 trillion and expanded its buyback to JPY1.3 trillion while lowering its vehicle-sales forecast. The shares rose 17%, the largest one-day gain since 1987. SG reads the result as hybrid mix, cost control and currency support driving profitability.

China: banks, over half of onshore earnings, reported resilient profits on loan growth, stable margins and cost control. Consumer earnings were mixed on weak household demand. Kweichow Moutai met expectations, the broader staples sector stayed in contraction, and consumer discretionary earnings fell 11% y/y, mainly on autos.

Pharma is a defensive source of upgrades. Pfizer raised revenue and earnings guidance as non-Covid product sales rose 7%, and 46 of 51 S&P 500 healthcare companies beat estimates. SG says the sector's improvement comes from new-product launches rather than higher capital spending or cyclical demand, unlike technology and industrials.

3Q26 global earnings vs consensus (1304 of 1662 companies reported): 644 companies (39%) above consensus, 292 (18%) in line, 368 (22%) below, 358 (21%) still to report. In line is defined as -3% to +3% vs Bloomberg consensus on adjusted EPS.

S&P 500 EPS surprise chart: 441 of 499 companies reported. Sales surprises: 440 of 499 reported. Percentage splits are given in the charts but the text does not label which share belongs to which category.

The report includes EPS and sales surprise breakdowns for STOXX 600 (247/335 EPS, 322/442 sales), STOXX 200 Small (62/86 EPS, 77/116 sales), TOPIX 500 (200/364 EPS, 253/460 sales) and CSI 300 (209/210 EPS, 199/200 sales), plus historic surprise series, 2026 and 2027 consensus EPS growth, and 3-month EPS revisions by region and sector.

AI-related results were very strong, but the stocks fell on regulatory risk tied to the US midterms.
European backlogs are not converting into margins and cash flow, as the Alstom and Rheinmetall warnings show.
Household demand is sluggish, staples earnings are still contracting and consumer discretionary earnings fell 11% y/y.
